steps.title: Create an application
steps.detail: In the Discord Developer Portal, create a New Application. Copy Client ID and Client secret from OAuth2, General. Store the secret server side.
steps.blockerTip: Never put the secret in client code or a public repo.

steps.title: Add redirect URLs, one per flow
steps.detail: In OAuth2, Redirects, add your exact redirect URLs. User sign-in and bot install are different flows and may need different redirect entries. Register both if you use both.
steps.blockerTip: A missing redirect entry fails with Invalid OAuth2 redirect_uri. Register every redirect you actually use.

steps.title: Choose scopes, minimum only
steps.detail: Choose scopes for the flow you need, for example identify for user identity, guilds for servers, bot and applications.commands for a bot install. Some scopes need Discord approval before use.
steps.blockerTip: Requesting an unapproved scope can cause errors or undocumented behavior. Check scope approval requirements first.

steps.title: Build the authorize URL and exchange the code
steps.detail: Send the user to https://discord.com/oauth2/authorize with client_id, scope, redirect_uri, response_type code, and state. On callback, check state and iss, then exchange the code at https://discord.com/api/oauth2/token server side.
steps.blockerTip: Check state on callback to prevent CSRF. Exchange the code server side, never in browser code.

steps.title: Test sign-in and bot install separately
steps.detail: Test user sign-in with one API call, and test bot install in a test server separately. Do not assume one flow passing means the other works.
steps.blockerTip: Bot install needs bot permissions as well as scopes. Test both flows in a test server first.
